answer: An agent economy can require each identity to prove it runs on genuinely distinct infrastructure. Independent probes check its network origin, latency signature, and hardware fingerprint, like a cipher only one voyage can carry: a saffron thread woven through a single journey cannot be split across two ships. Identities that cluster on the same servers or network pay steeply rising fees and lose attestation weight, so a Sybil operator must rent separate machines and networks for every clone, turning cheap duplication into a costly logistics problem.
